findings.text: The lane exposes helpers that translate a processor index into the identifier used for delivery. One helper returns the stored per processor mapping, another returns a single bit selected by the processor index, and a presence guarded helper returns the stored mapping when the index is within the allowed set and present else a sentinel bad value.

Boot option handling for verbosity distinguishes absent argument from named levels. With no argument the handler rejects on legacy width builds and otherwise clears the flag that disables the IO side and succeeds. With a debug word it selects debug verbosity and with a verbose word it selects verbose verbosity, while unrecognised words on wide builds warn and fail. Success is zero and failure is a negative invalid code.

External NMI delivery mode selection requires an argument and matches leading words for all, none, or boot processor only, storing the corresponding mode. Unknown words trigger a warning and report invalid input, while recognised words succeed.

Local APIC resource registration fails when no memory base is established. Otherwise it covers one page starting at the base and inserts the descriptor into the global memory resource map, then reports success.
Default logical destination setup selects flat destination format then merges a logical identifier derived from the current processor into the destination register while preserving other bits.

The physical flat driver claims every platform during probe and OEM validation, operates in physical destination mode, and uses native memory operations for register access, end of interrupt, and interrupt command handling with blocking and timeout bounded waits. It derives the destination from the stored per processor mapping and permits NMI to offline processors. The global driver pointer defaults to this table and is frozen after init.

The noop driver provides inert inter processor signalling where all directed, masked, and broadcast sends do nothing, reads return zero, writes do nothing, end of interrupt does nothing, command reads return zero, and secondary wakeup reports failure. It declares logical destination mode and uses the single bit processor mapping for destination calculation.
Noop register access warns once when the boot processor advertises APIC hardware while the disabled flag is clear, signalling unexpected use of the inert path on capable hardware.

Driver tables share a common shape with identity and selection callbacks, a logical mode flag, an error status disable flag, presence translation and identifier limit and extraction and destination calculation callbacks, a family of send callbacks covering single, mask, mask excluding self, all excluding self, all, and self, an optional secondary wakeup callback, an offline NMI flag in some variants, and a register operation group for read, write, end of interrupt, command read and write, and command idle waits.

Numachip identifier extraction has two platform variants that both start from the high byte of the supplied value. The first variant merges node identity from a node MSR when the related feature is enabled, while the second merges fabric address bits from a memory configuration MSR. Both widen the usable space beyond the flat limit.

Numachip remote signalling is funnelled through a function pointer installed during system init, with per generation register addresses and field placements. Secondary start uses that path to emit an init pulse followed by a startup pulse carrying the shifted start address, then reports success.

Single target delivery on Numachip compares the high portion of the target and local identifiers under disabled preemption. On match it uses the local APIC destination path with interrupts masked across the programming sequence, otherwise it writes the fabric controller with NMI delivery for the NMI vector and fixed delivery otherwise.

The local path of Numachip single delivery runs with preemption disabled and restores it on both outcomes, and additionally masks local interrupts only around the local controller programming, preventing migration and reentrancy during identifier comparison and register update.

Numachip collective sends iterate over the supplied mask or the online set and skip the caller where the variant excludes self, delegating each target to the single send path. Broadcast to all reuses the mask path over the online set, and self delivery writes the architectural self interrupt register.

Numachip generation probes succeed only when the global driver already points at the matching table. ACPI OEM validation matches vendor and table strings and records the generation on success, otherwise it declines. System init maps the generation specific control window, installs the matching fabric write helper, and hooks processor fixup and PCI init. Processor fixup records cache and package topology derived from the node input and nodes per socket when the node MSR feature is present.

Default destination based IPI first synchronises on command idle using a timeout tolerant wait for the NMI vector and a blocking wait otherwise, then programs the destination field and the vector with the requested mode.

Command idle synchronisation has two forms sharing the same busy test on the command register. One form retries with delay and retry accounting up to a bound and reports busy on exhaustion else success, while the other spins with relaxed waiting until idle with no timeout.

Command word assembly combines the supplied shortcut and destination mode with delivery semantics selected by vector, using NMI delivery for the NMI vector and fixed delivery with the vector number otherwise.
Hardware NMI sample period scales the processor clock rate by the supplied threshold through millisecond and second conversions, yielding a cycle count proportional to both inputs.

Architecture backtrace support raises NMI on a caller supplied mask through the APIC mask path, funnels exclusion handling through a generic helper, and resolves the local NMI action as handled when the generic backtrace routine consumes it else done.

Lane init entries run once during boot and include verbosity and external NMI option parsers, LAPIC resource insertion, Numachip probes and system init, backtrace handler registration, APIC static dispatch setup, IOAPIC disable parsing, early IOAPIC setup, PIRQ remapping setup, and IOAPIC diagnostic printing.

APIC static dispatch setup copies the current end of interrupt handler into the native slot, refreshes the static call sites, and logs completion. A helper macro declares null static call sites derived from driver callback names, and an override descriptor is reserved in init data.

IOAPIC bookkeeping centres on a mutex, a dynamic IRQ base, an initialised flag, a global count, a top global system interrupt, a fixed MP interrupt source table with entry count, a bus type table, and a disabled flag frozen after init. Per pin linkage, per IRQ chip data with pin list, saved route entry, level and polarity and ISA flags and reference count, global system interrupt ranges, and per IOAPIC descriptors with register count, saved state, MP config, routing info, domain config, domain pointer, and memory resource are also defined, with fixed size arrays for devices and two IRQ chip instances.

The IOAPIC register window exposes an index selector, a data port, and an end of interrupt port with reserved slots between them, accessed through memory mapped I/O. Reads select a register through the index port then fetch from the data port.

Early IOAPIC init marks all legacy interrupts as IOAPIC owned when no legacy interrupts exist, then allocates saved register state for every enumerated device and reports success. A boot option without arguments disables IOAPIC support entirely.

IOAPIC register updates and end of interrupt fan out hold a dedicated spinlock with interrupts saved, covering mask changes with a read fence and pin by pin acknowledgement. A separate mutex serialises higher level IOAPIC management, and a zap routine reinitialises the spinlock for suspend, resume, or kexec style reuse.

Pin bookkeeping removes the first list entry matching a given controller and pin and frees it, silently doing nothing when absent. Masking updates the hardware route under lock with a data read fence to order posted writes, and acknowledgement walks all pins attached to an IRQ vector under the same lock.

PCI interrupt resolution scans the MP interrupt table for entries matching bus, slot, and type on PCI capable buses, requires the destination controller to be enumerated or wildcard, skips ISA results, prefers an exact pin match while retaining the first pin mismatched candidate as a broken table fallback, and finally allocates a mapping for the chosen entry, reporting failure when no candidate exists.
Flat drivers cap the APIC identifier at 254 [CITED] while Numachip drivers allow the full unsigned range. Identifier extraction takes the top byte of the register value.
PIRQ remapping supports 8 [CITED] entries initialised to -1 [CITED] and filled in reverse order from boot options limited to the table size, handling faulty firmware tables.
Kernel log lines from this IOAPIC init file use an APIC prefix, and reverse enumeration starts at the last enumerated controller and steps down to the first.

IOAPIC diagnostics dump each redirection entry with enabled state, trigger type, polarity, vector, remote and status bits, and either remapping details or destination mode and identifiers and delivery mode. Controller header dumps read version gated registers under lock and skip phantom reads that repeat the previous value, while lock reset reinitialises the serialization primitive.
